claim: For every integer \(n>5040\) with \(\omega(n)=7\), the gap \(\Delta_7(n)=e^\gamma\sum_{j=0}^{7}(\ln\ln\ln n)^j/j!-\sigma(n)/n\) has a unique global minimum at \(n=367567200=2^5\cdot3^3\cdot5^2\cdot7\cdot11\cdot13\cdot17\), and \(0.1690<\Delta_7(n)<0.1691\) there.

correctness.rationale: The support-replacement argument reduces the global minimum to the first seven primes; the exact universal divisor-ratio bound and certified cutoff exclude every \(n\ge52{,}000{,}000{,}000\); the included interval checker verifies every one of the 2,596 remaining exponent tuples, with the candidate gap in (0.1690,0.1691) and every other gap above 0.1691.

evidence: The paper states the unconditional result for \(\omega(n)\le6\) and gives a finite candidate check for minimal-counterexample candidates with \(7\le\omega(n)\le20\); PDF lines 257–276 and 2644–2683.
The text says the check verifies the inequality, not the exact minimum gap over all integers with \(\omega(n)=7\).
broader_coverage.reasoning: Prior work covers the sign/positivity question more broadly, so the present claim is limited to a sharper quantitative invariant: the exact minimum margin and its unique attaining integer. The broader sign result alone does not imply this value or uniqueness.

value.rationale: This gives a sharp quantitative safety margin at the first prime-support layer beyond the paper’s elementary omega≤6 bound, and identifies the unique extremizer rather than merely verifying positivity. The margin and extremizer provide a reproducible benchmark for the strength of the truncation. The result is deliberately restricted to \(\omega(n)=7\).
